generatedProse.concept-context: In practice, this means handling sources the same connected way on every piece of work, in any subject. You choose a style, cite each source as you write, build a matching reference, and keep the whole list consistent. The in-text citation and the reference list are two ends of one thread, held together by the style. Doing all three as one practice, on every assignment, is what keeps your referencing accurate.
generatedProse.worked-example: Two students each write a piece that draws on several sources. One treats referencing as separate jobs: they cite as they go, but build the list in a rush at the end, and it mixes styles and misses entries. The other runs it as one practice: one style chosen first, each source cited and given a matching reference, and a final check of the whole list. Both read the same sources, but only the second student's referencing holds together under a marker's eye.
generatedProse.summary: Referencing is most useful when you treat it as one connected practice, not three separate jobs. You run the same parts in order on every piece: choose a style, cite each source, build a matching reference, and check the whole list is consistent. It is handling all three as one practice, assignment after assignment, that keeps your referencing accurate.

check.body: A student chooses one style, cites each source as they write by quoting or paraphrasing, builds a matching reference for each, and checks the list is consistent before handing in. What does this show?

feedback.correct: That's right. Using feedback to plan the next piece of work feeds it straight back into your learning, closing the loop and starting the next round stronger. That is the cycle working as it should.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Think about what the student did with the feedback, and what improved as a result.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Acting on feedback feeds your next round of learning and preparation, which is why the following essay was stronger. The mark on the first essay cannot change, but the feedback still shapes what comes next.

_items.text: That the student is using referencing as one practice: each part connects, from the citation to the reference to the consistent style.
_items.feedback: Yes. Every part is there, connected, working as one practice.

_items.text: That the student is doing far more than any piece of work needs.
_items.feedback: No. Each part does a different job, and together they make the referencing sound.

_items.text: That only the final check at the end really matters.
_items.feedback: Not so. The earlier parts did the real work; the check only confirms it.

_items.text: That citing and building references are the same step.
_items.feedback: They are different parts: you cite as you write, and build the full reference for the list.

_prompts.concept-context: What does this look like in practice within the given context? Write a short follow-on from the generic definition above, in the learner's own subject or discipline. Keep it to two or three sentences, mid-register, following straight on from the generic definition.
_prompts.worked-example: Give a subject-specific worked example of this lesson's concept: a weaker or less-developed version first, then a stronger version reached by better practice, using the context cast (character tokens) consistently. Keep the weaker-then-stronger shape and the two-part contrast; name the cast directly in the prose (the pack supplies the whole body). The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
_prompts.summary: Recap what the learner can now do, in terms of their own subject or context. One short paragraph. Do not restate the learning outcomes verbatim.
_prompts.check: Write the subject's own version of this lesson's check question(s), testing the same outcome in the learner's own discipline. Keep the same number of items and the same correctness pattern as the generic version; reword the stem and items for the subject. Keep the component-level feedback (correct / notFinal / final) teaching, never a bare verdict.
